summary: The api component is the reason/LLM-IO stage: ApiClient sends the Message history to the model via chat (blocking) or chat_stream (SSE), returning a ChatResponse with Choices and Usage. tool_calling extracts ToolCalls from native tool_calls or by robustly parsing model text, attach_tools puts ToolDefinitions on the request, and message canonicalization/sanitization keeps the wire format valid. Retry, circuit breaker, and a latched wall-clock budget guard every billable call.
context_basis: recommendations were formed with src/api/ read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), grounded in client.rs ApiClient/chat/chat_stream/RetryConfig, types.rs Message/ChatResponse/Usage/ToolCall, streaming.rs StreamChunk, and tool_calling.rs extract_tool_calls/attach_tools.

examples.title: Send the history and get a ChatResponse
examples.intent: Produce one model turn from the current conversation state.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApiClient::chat posts the Message history and returns a ChatResponse whose first Choice carries the assistant Message; this is the reason step that yields either text or tool calls for the act stage.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the Reason node fires a single request and lands the response card beneath it.
touch_interaction.visual: The node spins while in flight and settles green when the ChatResponse arrives.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop sends the history to chat, gets an assistant Message with two tool calls, and hands them to dispatch.
examples.pitfall: Sending a history with no user message can trigger a provider 400; canonicalization must inject one first.

examples.title: Stream a turn with chat_stream
examples.intent: Render partial output and tool calls as they arrive rather than blocking to completion.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: chat_stream yields a StreamingResponse whose channel emits StreamChunk::Content/Reasoning/ToolCall/Usage/FinishReason, letting the loop show progress and start act preparation before the turn finishes.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the Reason node opens a live token stream lane that fills left to right as chunks arrive.
touch_interaction.visual: Content chunks type out in real time; a ToolCall chunk pops a tool chip onto the lane.

examples.mini_scenario: The model streams reasoning then a tool call; the UI shows the text live and the loop queues the tool as it lands.
examples.pitfall: Failing to accumulate ToolCallDelta fragments by index yields a truncated, unparseable tool call.

examples.title: Attach ToolDefinitions to the request
examples.intent: Tell the model which tools it may call this turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: attach_tools sets body.tools from the ToolDefinitions and, when native function calling is on, sets tool_choice=auto, shaping the model's available act surface for the reason turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws edges from tool nodes into the Reason node to declare which tools this turn exposes.
touch_interaction.visual: Attached tools show a small plug icon on the Reason node's rim.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop attaches the critical tool definitions so the model can emit a native tool call.
examples.pitfall: Attaching the full tool catalog every turn wastes context; attach only what the turn needs.

examples.title: Extract tool calls, native first
examples.intent: Get structured ToolCalls out of the model turn regardless of format.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: extract_tool_calls reads message.tool_calls when present and otherwise falls back to extract_tool_calls_from_text, so both native-FC and text-only models feed the same act stage.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the response card splits out the tool-call chips it contains.
touch_interaction.visual: Native calls render with a solid plug icon; text-parsed calls render with a dashed 'recovered' icon.

examples.mini_scenario: A model without native FC emits a JSON block in text; extract_tool_calls_from_text recovers the ToolCall.
examples.pitfall: Assuming native tool_calls exist for every model drops the calls of text-only backends entirely.

examples.title: Robustly parse tool calls from text
examples.intent: Recover tool calls even when the model wraps them in prose or slightly malformed JSON.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: extract_tool_calls_from_text delegates to the tool_parser and parsed_to_tool_call assigns a synthetic id (parsed_<uuid>), so imperfect model output still becomes a valid ToolCall for the act stage.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a recovered tool chip shows the raw text it was parsed from.
touch_interaction.visual: Recovered chips carry a repair-wrench badge and a tooltip with the source span.

examples.mini_scenario: The model emits a fenced JSON tool call inside a paragraph; the parser extracts it and the loop runs it.
examples.pitfall: Assigning a non-unique synthetic id collides tool results and breaks call-to-result pairing.

examples.title: Feed a tool result back as a tool message
examples.intent: Close the act-to-reason loop by returning execution output to the model.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Message::tool(content, tool_call_id) binds role='tool' with the result JSON so the next chat turn perceives the outcome and reasons about the next move.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws an edge from a tool result card back into the Message history strip feeding the next turn.
touch_interaction.visual: The tool message renders as a distinct grey bubble tagged with its call id.

examples.mini_scenario: cargo_test output is wrapped as a tool message keyed to its call id and the model reads it next turn.
examples.pitfall: A tool message whose tool_call_id does not match any prior call is rejected by strict providers.

examples.title: Canonicalize message order
examples.intent: Keep the request in a shape providers accept.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: canonicalize_message_order enforces system-first, merges multiple system messages, and injects a dummy user message if missing, so the reason turn never fails a 400 on ordering.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks the history strip to auto-sort system messages to the top and merge duplicates.
touch_interaction.visual: System bubbles slide to the front and collapse into a single pinned card.

examples.mini_scenario: A history with two system messages and no user turn is normalized before the request so it is accepted.
examples.pitfall: Skipping canonicalization on resumed histories can send an out-of-order payload that the provider rejects.

examples.title: Sanitize empty assistant content
examples.intent: Avoid provider 400s when the assistant turn has no visible text.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: sanitize_assistant_content replaces empty assistant content with the reasoning trace or a placeholder, so tool-only turns still form a valid Message for the next request.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping an empty assistant bubble fills it with the reasoning summary or a placeholder marker.
touch_interaction.visual: Empty bubbles show a hollow outline that fills solid once sanitized.

examples.mini_scenario: A tool-only assistant turn has empty content; sanitization inserts the reasoning so the next request is valid.
examples.pitfall: Leaving assistant content empty makes some providers 400 and stalls the loop mid-turn.

examples.title: Account tokens with Usage
examples.intent: Track how much budget each reason turn consumes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The ChatResponse carries Usage (prompt/completion/total tokens plus optional cost); the loop adds it to the cumulative budget that guards iteration and wall-clock stops.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the Reason node reveals a token meter for the last turn and the running total.
touch_interaction.visual: A dual bar shows prompt vs completion tokens; it deepens red as the cumulative total climbs.

examples.mini_scenario: Each turn's Usage is summed so the loop knows when it is nearing its token budget.
examples.pitfall: Trusting an unvalidated Usage where total != prompt + completion corrupts budget accounting.

examples.title: Capture request metadata with ChatMetadata
examples.intent: Record exactly what was sent and how the turn resolved.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: chat_with_meta / chat_stream_with_meta return ChatMetadata (request_body, elapsed_ms, finish_reason, token counts, cost), giving the learn stage a full trace of each reason turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the Reason node opens a metadata drawer with the request body and timing.
touch_interaction.visual: A ledger badge shows elapsed ms and finish_reason; slow turns glow amber.

examples.mini_scenario: A turn is logged with its finish_reason and elapsed_ms so a stall can later be diagnosed.
examples.pitfall: Logging the raw request_body without redacting the api_key leaks the credential into the trace.

examples.title: Retry retryable failures with backoff
examples.intent: Survive transient 429/5xx without failing the whole turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RetryConfig retries retryable_status_codes with exponential backoff plus jitter and honors Retry-After, so a flaky provider does not immediately push the loop into ErrorRecovery.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the Reason node opens the retry policy dial for max attempts and delays.
touch_interaction.visual: During retries the node shows a countdown ring for the backoff window.

examples.mini_scenario: A 429 with Retry-After makes the client wait the advised interval then retry, and the turn succeeds.
examples.pitfall: Retrying a non-idempotent request without care can double-submit; only retry safe status classes.

examples.title: Trip the circuit breaker on repeated failure
examples.intent: Stop hammering a backend that is clearly down.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CircuitBreaker wraps calls and opens after repeated failures, returning CircuitBreakerError fast so the loop fails cleanly instead of burning budget on doomed requests.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the Reason node shows the breaker state (closed/open) as a switch on its rim.
touch_interaction.visual: The breaker switch flips red and the node greys out when open.

examples.mini_scenario: After several consecutive backend failures the breaker opens and the next request short-circuits immediately.
examples.pitfall: Setting the breaker threshold too tight opens on ordinary transient blips and starves the loop of turns.

examples.title: Latch the wall-clock budget on the first call
examples.intent: Bound total LLM-IO time even across retries and multiple turns.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The wall-clock deadline is latched on the first billable request and shared across all retries/calls; once expired, WallClockBudgetExceeded is raised before any new request as a budget stop, not a network error.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating a dial on the Reason node sets the shared wall-clock ceiling for all LLM I/O.
touch_interaction.visual: A clock ring shared across turns drains and locks red when the deadline passes.

examples.mini_scenario: Mid-turn the wall budget expires; the next request is refused with WallClockBudgetExceeded classified as a budget stop.
examples.pitfall: Classifying a wall-budget stop as a network error mislabels the failure mode and may trigger pointless retries.

examples.title: Handle context overflow explicitly
examples.intent: React to a too-large request by compacting rather than dying.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApiError::ContextOverflow signals the request exceeded the window, letting the loop trigger compression and retry the reason turn with a smaller history.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: On overflow the history strip auto-pinches, folding old turns before the request is retried.
touch_interaction.visual: The node flashes an overflow badge, then the history visibly shrinks and the turn re-fires.

examples.mini_scenario: A large history returns ContextOverflow; the loop runs compact_auto and resends within the window.
examples.pitfall: Treating ContextOverflow like a generic error retries the same oversized payload and fails again.

examples.title: Configure thinking mode
examples.intent: Control how much hidden reasoning the model spends per turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ThinkingMode (Enabled/Disabled/Budget(n)) shapes the reasoning depth of each turn, trading token spend for deliberation on hard steps.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the Reason node dials thinking from off to a token budget for deeper reasoning.
touch_interaction.visual: Higher thinking deepens the node color and shows a separate reasoning stream lane.

examples.mini_scenario: For a tricky refactor the loop sets Budget(4000) so the model reasons harder before acting.
examples.pitfall: Leaving a large thinking budget on for trivial turns wastes tokens the loop budget cannot spare.

examples.title: Collect a streamed turn into a full response
examples.intent: Reassemble streamed chunks into a single canonical assistant Message.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: StreamingResponse::collect drains the StreamChunk stream and accumulates tool-call deltas and content into one ChatResponse, so downstream code treats streamed and blocking turns identically.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the stream lane collapses the chunk trail into a single settled response card.
touch_interaction.visual: Chunks converge and merge into one card with a completion checkmark.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop streams for UI but collects the chunks into a ChatResponse before running the recovered tool calls.
examples.pitfall: Reading content chunks but ignoring the accumulator loses tool-call fragments spread across deltas.

examples.title: Guard the credential endpoint before authorizing
examples.intent: Never send the API key to an unsafe or spoofed endpoint.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Before attaching the Authorization header the client asserts the endpoint is safe, so the reason turn cannot leak the key over plaintext HTTP or to a lookalike host.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the Reason node shows the endpoint safety check gating the key attachment.
touch_interaction.visual: A green padlock appears for safe endpoints; unsafe ones show a red broken lock and block the send.

examples.mini_scenario: The endpoint is a plaintext remote host; the guard refuses to attach the key and the turn is blocked.
examples.pitfall: Attaching the key before the endpoint safety check can exfiltrate the credential in a single request.

examples.title: Read cost from the usage field
examples.intent: Track real dollar cost per turn where the provider reports it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: For OpenRouter the request sets usage.include=true and the response usage.cost feeds the cumulative cost that the loop's max_cost guard watches.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the Reason node flips the token meter to a running dollar cost readout.
touch_interaction.visual: A currency badge accumulates per turn and reddens as it approaches the cost ceiling.

examples.mini_scenario: Each OpenRouter turn reports usage.cost, which the loop sums to enforce a spending cap.
examples.pitfall: Assuming every provider returns usage.cost yields a zero-cost illusion on backends that omit it.

examples.title: Map HTTP status to a typed ApiError
examples.intent: Turn raw HTTP failures into loop-actionable error kinds.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApiError variants (Network, HttpStatus, ContextOverflow, Timeout) let the loop route each failure to the right response: retry, compact, recover, or fail.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a failed response card reveals its typed error kind and the routing it triggers.
touch_interaction.visual: Each error kind has a distinct icon: cloud-off for Network, clock for Timeout, overflow for ContextOverflow.

examples.mini_scenario: A Timeout is routed to a retry while a ContextOverflow is routed to compaction, each handled distinctly.
examples.pitfall: Collapsing all failures into a generic error robs the loop of the signal it needs to respond correctly.

examples.title: Mock the client for deterministic loops
examples.intent: Drive the loop with scripted turns so behavior is testable without a real backend.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The api mock implements the same client seam and returns canned ChatResponses, letting the whole loop state machine be exercised deterministically offline.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the Reason node in test mode swaps the live backend for a scripted stub node.
touch_interaction.visual: The node shows a test-tube badge and renders scripted responses without a spinner.

examples.mini_scenario: A test scripts a two-turn tool sequence through the mock to assert the loop transitions correctly.
examples.pitfall: A mock that skips canonicalization/sanitization hides wire-format bugs that only bite against the real API.
